html:
On 1 July 1867 the British North America Act united the colonies of Canada, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick into the Dominion of Canada, with four provinces: Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick. Ottawa was the capital.

Leaders such as John A. Macdonald and George-Etienne Cartier planned it at conferences in Charlottetown and Quebec in 1864. They feared American expansion after the Civil War and wanted a railway and a larger market.

The new country soon grew: it bought Rupert's Land from the Hudson's Bay Company in 1870, which led to the rising of Louis Riel, and British Columbia joined in 1871 on the promise of the Pacific railway. Canada Day is kept on 1 July. Full legal independence came only in 1982, with the Charter.
sum: On 1 July 1867 the British North America Act united the colonies of Canada, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick into the Dominion of Canada, with four provinces: Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick. Ottawa was the capital.
